# /docs — page templates, generation markers, source footers

Conventions + the three page templates. Everything `/docs` writes follows the marker and
footer rules below; the templates are skeletons — fill only the sections a real source
covers (or a `user-confirmed` answer), drop the rest.

---

## Generation-marker convention

Every generated region sits between a begin/end HTML-comment pair keyed by a stable
section id:

```markdown
<!-- docs:begin:getting-started — generated by /docs; refresh with /docs readme. Hand edits inside this block will be overwritten; write outside the markers instead. -->
…generated content…
<!-- docs:end:getting-started -->
```

Rules:
- **Section ids are stable kebab-case** (listed per template below). Never rename an id on
  refresh — the id is how update mode finds the region.
- **Refresh = replace strictly between the markers**, in place. Everything outside any
  marker pair is hand-written territory — never touched, never reordered.
- **One marker pair per section id per file.** A duplicate id on read is a corruption —
  surface it to the user instead of guessing which to refresh.
- Feature-guide and api pages are *mostly* generated, but still use per-section markers so
  a human can interleave hand-written sections (a tips block, a screenshot) that survive
  regeneration.
- An existing README **without markers** is hand-written: draft the owned sections, show
  the user exactly where each would go (after which heading / replacing which section), and
  insert markers only where they approve. Never silently rewrite.

## Source-footer convention

Last line(s) of every generated page — and of each README owned section — an HTML comment:

```markdown
<!-- sources: .ai/specs/checkout/prd.md · .ai/specs/checkout/ux.md · .human/specs/checkout/prd.md
     user-confirmed: "support email is help@example.com" (2026-06-10)
     note: written while feature status was `building` (user approved early docs) -->
```

- `sources:` — every artifact path a claim in the region traces to.
- `user-confirmed:` — one line per spec-silent fact the user supplied, quoted, dated.
- `note:` — only for caveats worth keeping (early-docs warning per SKILL.md rule 4).
- The footer is the ONLY place chain internals may appear. The prose above it never names
  PRDs, specs, slices, or artifact paths.

---

## Template 1 — root `README.md` (`/docs readme`)

Owned section ids: `what-this-is` · `getting-started` · `project-layout` ·
`running-tests`. Title + badges + anything else are hand-written territory.

````markdown
# <Project name — ask if intake doesn't settle it>

<!-- docs:begin:what-this-is … -->
<One-paragraph plain answer: what the app does and who it's for — from intake's one-liner +
discovery's problem/target user. No roadmap, no architecture talk.>
<!-- sources: .ai/intake.md · .human/intake/idea.md · .ai/discovery/<slug>.md -->
<!-- docs:end:what-this-is -->

<!-- docs:begin:getting-started … -->
## Getting started

**Prerequisites:** <runtime + major version from anchor stack; tools bootstrap assumes>

```bash
<install command — verbatim from bootstrap dev scripts>
<env setup — "copy .env.example to .env and fill in:" + variable NAMES from environments (never values)>
<run command — verbatim from bootstrap>
```

<Where it's running once up — dev URL/port from environments' dev env.>
<!-- sources: .ai/anchor.md · .ai/bootstrap.md · .ai/environments.md -->
<!-- docs:end:getting-started -->

<!-- docs:begin:project-layout … -->
## Project layout

| Folder | What lives there |
| :-- | :-- |
| `<dir from bootstrap/disk>` | <the architecture component's role, in plain English> |
<!-- sources: .ai/architecture[.md|/] 02-components · .ai/bootstrap.md -->
<!-- docs:end:project-layout -->

<!-- docs:begin:running-tests … -->
## Running tests

```bash
<test command — verbatim from test-strategy>
```

<One or two lines on the suite shape — unit/integration/e2e and where they live — only if
test-strategy states it.>
<!-- sources: .ai/test-strategy.md -->
<!-- docs:end:running-tests -->
````

Tier notes: prototype README = these four sections, lean (a missing-source section is
simply skipped). mvp+ may add a `## Documentation` line linking `docs/` pages once they
exist (id: `docs-index`).

---

## Template 2 — feature guide `docs/<feature>.md` (`/docs <feature>`)

Owned section ids: `overview` · `how-to` · `what-youll-see` · `limits`. Audience:
discovery's target user. Task-oriented, second person, everyday entity terms from
`.ai/context.md`. Zero internal jargon; sources only in footers.

````markdown
# <Feature, named as the user would say it — from the features.md title / PRD JTBD, not the slug>

<!-- docs:begin:overview … -->
<What this lets you do and when you'd use it — 2–4 sentences from the PRD problem + JTBD +
in-scope list. Capabilities only; nothing the scope doesn't include.>
<!-- docs:end:overview -->

<!-- docs:begin:how-to … -->
## How to use it

<One `### <Task in the user's words>` block per PRD user story (group small ones). UI
features: numbered steps walked from ux.md's flow for that story — screen by screen, naming
buttons/labels with ux.md's verbatim copy. Non-UI features: the user-visible action and
result, still end-user voiced.>

### <Task>
1. <step — from ux flow>
2. <step>
<What's true when you're done — the story's outcome.>
<!-- docs:end:how-to -->

<!-- docs:begin:what-youll-see … -->
## What you'll see

<Only states ux.md specs: the empty state ("Before you add anything, you'll see …" — verbatim
empty-state copy), what errors look like (verbatim error copy + what to do), loading
behavior if notable. Skip entirely for non-UI features with no ux.md.>
<!-- docs:end:what-youll-see -->

<!-- docs:begin:limits … -->
## Limits

<Plain bullets from the PRD's out-of-scope / non-goals that an end user would bump into.
Phrase as "X isn't supported (yet)" — never as roadmap promises.>
<!-- docs:end:limits -->

<!-- sources: .ai/specs/<feature>/prd.md · .ai/specs/<feature>/ux.md · .human/specs/<feature>/prd.md
     user-confirmed: … -->
````

## Template 3 — API reference `docs/api.md` (`/docs api [feature]`)

One file; one marker-owned section per feature that has contracts (id:
`api-<feature-slug>`), plus a shared `api-overview` section. `/docs api <feature>`
regenerates only that feature's section. Audience: an external developer — API jargon is
fine here, chain jargon still isn't. **Every row renders from `design.md § API contracts`;
a missing piece is a `BLOCKED-ON-DESIGN` bounce, never a guess.**

````markdown
# API reference

<!-- docs:begin:api-overview … -->
**Base URL:** `<from environments.md roster — per env if several>`
**Authentication:** <scheme from design contracts / anchor auth — how to present credentials>
**Versioning:** <design's versioning strategy — present at production>
<!-- sources: .ai/environments.md · .ai/anchor.md -->
<!-- docs:end:api-overview -->

<!-- docs:begin:api-<feature-slug> … -->
## <Feature, plainly named>

### `<METHOD> <path>`

<One sentence: what it does — from the contract row's purpose.>

**Auth:** <required scheme/scope> · **Idempotency:** <from the contract — state-changing endpoints>

**Request**

```json
<request shape from the contract table — field, type, required>
```

**Response `<2xx>`**

```json
<response shape>
```

**Errors**

| Status | Shape / code | When |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| <4xx/5xx — EVERY error shape the contract lists> | <body shape> | <condition> |

<!-- sources: .ai/specs/<feature-slug>/design.md -->
<!-- docs:end:api-<feature-slug> -->
````

---

## Voice checklist (run before writing any page)

- [ ] Reader = discovery's target user (api target: an external developer) — not the chain.
- [ ] No "PRD", "spec", "slice", "invariant", "artifact", "tier" in prose.
- [ ] Every command copy-pasteable and sourced (bootstrap / test-strategy / real files on disk).
- [ ] Every UI label/message verbatim from ux.md — no paraphrased button names.
- [ ] No secret values; env vars by NAME + `.env.example` pointer.
- [ ] No roadmap promises; limits phrased as today's behavior.
- [ ] Every section has a source or a `user-confirmed` line — otherwise it isn't written.
